images.title: A rhombus is half its rectangle
images.purpose: Shows a rhombus with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm inside the 20 cm by 15 cm rectangle, filling exactly half of it.
images.composition: One rhombus, large and centred, inside a dashed rectangle drawn round its diagonals.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A grey (#6B7280) dashed rectangle 20 units wide and 15 units tall. Inside it, a rhombus whose corners are the midpoints of the four sides of the rectangle, filled teal (#0072B2). Its two diagonals drawn as grey dashed lines: horizontal 20 units, vertical 15 units, crossing at the centre with a small right angle mark. The four corner triangles of the rectangle outside the rhombus are left white. Labels: 20 cm under the horizontal diagonal near the centre; 15 cm beside the vertical diagonal; 150 cm² inside the rhombus in the upper left quarter. Check: 20 × 15 = 300 and 1/2 × 300 = 150.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The rhombus fills half the rectangle on its diagonals: 1/2 × 20 × 15 = 150 cm².
images.description: Shows a rhombus with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm inside the 20 cm by 15 cm rectangle, filling exactly half of it.
images.context: Practice concept; matches the exercise with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm.
images.teaching_notes: Point at the white corners: together they match the teal rhombus.

image_decisions.why: The half is visible: the rhombus and the white corners are equal, so the full product is twice too big.
